title: Slow-cooked spicy tomato beef stew
summary: A rich tomato beef stew with a gentle chilli kick and a splash of cream at the end. Serves 6. Takes about 30 minutes to prep, then 3 hours in the oven or 8 in a slow cooker.
source: The bot's own recipe, not taken from a website

parts.text: Serves 6.
Prep about 30 minutes. Cook 2.5 to 3 hours in the oven, or 8 hours on low in a slow cooker. It's even better the next day.
The beef

1.2 kg beef chuck or gravy beef, cut into 4 cm chunks
2 tbsp plain flour
Salt and pepper
3 tbsp olive oil
The base

2 brown onions, sliced
2 carrots, cut chunky
2 celery sticks, sliced
1 red capsicum, sliced
4 garlic cloves, crushed
2 tbsp tomato paste
The spice

2 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp ground cumin
1 to 2 tsp chilli flakes, or 1 fresh red chilli, chopped (1 tsp is mild, 2 is a decent kick)
1 tsp dried oregano or thyme
2 bay leaves
The sauce

2 tins (400 g each) crushed tomatoes
250 ml beef stock
125 ml red wine, or more stock
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
1 tsp brown sugar
To finish

100 ml thickened cream, or sour cream
A handful of chopped parsley
1. Coat the beef.
Toss the beef with the flour and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
2. Brown it.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole pot over high heat. Brown the beef in batches, 3 to 4 minutes a batch, then set it aside. Don't crowd the pot, or the beef steams instead of browning.
3. Soften the veg.
Turn the heat down to medium. Cook the onion, carrot, celery and capsicum for about 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, tomato paste, paprika, cumin, chilli and herbs and stir for a minute or two.
4. Build the sauce.
Pour in the wine and scrape the brown bits off the bottom. Add the tomatoes, stock, Worcestershire, sugar and bay leaves, then put the beef and its juices back in.
5. Slow cook.

Bring it to a simmer, put the lid on and cook until the beef falls apart. That's 2.5 to 3 hours in a 160°C oven, or on the lowest flame on the stovetop with a stir now and then. In a slow cooker, it's 8 hours on low or 4 to 5 on high.
6. Thicken and taste.
If it's too thin, take the lid off for the last 20 to 30 minutes. Fish out the bay leaves. Taste it and add more salt or chilli if you want.
7. Add the cream.
Take it off the heat and stir the cream through. Don't let it boil after that, or the cream can split. Scatter the parsley on top.
Creamy mash, crusty bread, rice or wide pasta like pappardelle.

blocks.title: Tips
blocks.text: For smokier heat, swap some of the chilli flakes for a chipotle in adobo. It freezes well: freeze it before the cream goes in, and add the cream when you reheat it.
